alternatives_and_why: Plan-A/B re-derivation reads the file at ROOT / rules.GATEB_VERDICT['path'], not the path stored in plan.json: the stored path is the CLI argument (often relative to the caller's cwd), and the pin's path is the committed file. A full re-derivation was chosen over storing a signature or a hash of the record: plan.json is writable by hand, so only the pinned file can be the source.

The cert pod in the floor is built from the fixed G4/J11-J14 shape with rules.job_record, the same call build_block makes, rather than a typed cost: the floor then follows any change to the timing rules.

Diagnostics/LN-12/judge pods were not given a pre-set floor shape: the kit has no fixed packing for them (the lead's jobs file), so any pre-set would be an invented plan; raised as open question 1 instead.
c0 stays optional on the cert pod (round 2's behaviour; the tests plan C1-C3 without c0 when no branch exists); only C1 and C2 are required, as VG2-3 asks.
open_questions_to_gpt: 1. §20 point 1 also names block A's diagnostics and judge pods (and LN-12 belongs to block A). They have no pre-set shape, so S1-0's floor excludes them; init-block A then counts them and refuses on a short event. Options: (a) accept as a stated limit (the lead tops up once with a margin above $103.53); (b) add an optional 'init-block S1-0 --block-a-jobs FILE' so the lead's block-A jobs file (diagnostics, LN-12, judge launches) is counted in S1-0's floor. (b) is more work and needs gates that do not yet apply before S1-0; I did not build it.

2. Under Branch 128 the arm pods are cheaper, but S1-0 is always planned before the branch exists, so the floor uses Branch full ($103.53). This over-asks by up to $5.79 if W1-18 passes; it is the conservative side and unchanged from round 2's rule.
